summary: Sir Trevor Mallard is a New Zealand politician and diplomat. He was born in Wellington on 17 June 1954. He trained and worked as a teacher. He joined the Labour Party in 1972. He was an MP from 1984 to 1990. He returned to Parliament from 1993 to 2022. He represented Hamilton West, Pencarrow and Hutt South. He was a list MP from 2017 to 2022. He was a Cabinet minister from 1999 to 2008. He was Minister of Education and of State Services for six years. Teachers' unions strongly criticised his education record. A school closure programme was stopped after heavy criticism. In 2007 he punched National MP Tau Henare. He pleaded guilty to fighting in a public place. He was Speaker of the House from 2017 to 2022. As Speaker he made Parliament more family-friendly. He dropped the requirement for male MPs to wear ties. Some of his actions drew criticism, including during the 2022 Wellington protests. He became ambassador to Ireland in February 2023. Foreign Minister Winston Peters recalled him in August 2025.
